brief: SOX is breaking through key short-term resistance into near-uncharted territory, but is only modestly overbought, not at the extreme levels a full squeeze typically reaches, implying room to run. Taiwan continues to lead the semiconductor trade, with SOX still lagging. The technical setup sits on a fundamental backdrop the note calls unusually strong: JPM's memory work sees supply/demand tightness persisting through 2028, with Micron's CY27/28 outlook even tighter than CY26, as demand outruns supply, cleanroom capacity stays constrained, and HBM demand grows faster than conventional server DRAM. Citing GS data, the note flags Taiwan server ODM revenues up 130% YoY, Aspeed up 118% YoY, and Korean DRAM exports up 412% YoY to a record, with DDR5/DDR4 spot prices trading above contract prices. GS also notes washed-out memory and HBM pricing expectations are now recovering, with more investors looking for upside. The combination of reset expectations, improving fundamentals and a technical breakout is framed as a setup for a squeeze, played via SOX options structures, where volatility is not cheap but is more reasonably priced than during the prior mania.
